# Design Principles

## Layout Consistency
- Use a predictable grid and alignment system across screens.
- Keep spacing and positioning consistent between similar views.
- Group related content visually and separate unrelated content clearly.
- Prefer balanced layouts that support scanning and task completion.

## Spacing System
- Use a small, repeatable spacing scale throughout the project.
- Keep padding, margins, and gaps consistent for equivalent elements.
- Avoid arbitrary spacing values unless a clear exception is needed.
- Preserve enough whitespace to improve readability without wasting space.

## Typography Hierarchy
- Establish a clear hierarchy for headings, body text, labels, and helper text.
- Use font size, weight, and line height intentionally to guide attention.
- Keep text styles consistent for the same semantic role.
- Prioritize legibility over decorative typography choices.

## Color Usage
- Use color purposefully for structure, state, and emphasis.
- Keep the palette restrained and consistent across the interface.
- Ensure sufficient contrast for all text and interactive elements.
- Do not rely on color alone to communicate status or meaning.

## Accessibility
- Design for keyboard access, screen readers, and high-contrast readability.
- Ensure interactive elements are large enough and clearly identifiable.
- Provide visible focus states and meaningful labels.
- Treat accessibility as a default requirement, not an exception.

## Component Consistency
- Reuse established patterns for buttons, forms, navigation, and feedback states.
- Keep component behavior, spacing, and styling consistent across contexts.
- Prefer composable, predictable components over one-off visual treatments.
- Avoid introducing new patterns unless they solve a real user need.

## Clarity and Usability
- Favor simple interfaces that help users complete tasks quickly.
- Reduce visual noise and remove unnecessary decoration.
- Make primary actions obvious and secondary actions unobtrusive.
- Keep content and controls easy to scan, understand, and use.
